V2 canManage() grants manage to admins that only have the VIEW scope on all groups

`canManage()` calls `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so an admin whose all-groups permission has only the `view` scope passes `canManage()`. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` guards creation with `auth.groups().requireManage()` (GroupsResource.java:181), so a view-only admin can create top-level groups, or move an existing group to top level by passing an id. The V1 `canManage()` and the rule 'manage requires manage' both say this should check only `MANAGE`. The javadoc added in GroupPermissionEvaluator (lines 75-76) repeats the VIEW-or-MANAGE wording, so it needs the same fix. Suggested fix: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`. `testManageAllGroups` only uses MANAGE and `testViewGroups` never tries a write, so no test catches this.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns resource UUIDs of the 'Groups' type resource, not group IDs

Per-group resources are created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-127). That method names the resource with the group id and never calls `setType`. Only the all-groups type resource (created at AdminPermissionsSchema.java:271-274) has type `Groups`. So `findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` visits just that one type resource. The lambda then passes `groupResource.getId()`, the internal resource UUID, to `hasPermission(groupId, ...)`. That does `findByName(server, groupId)`, which finds nothing and falls back to the all-groups evaluation. When all-groups has `view-members` or `manage-members`, the set gets the type resource's UUID, which is not a group id. Otherwise the set is empty. Callers: `UsersResource.searchForUser` sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ids)` when the set is non-empty. `JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery` (JpaUserProvider.java:1059-1089) then restricts users to members of those group ids, and also requires a resource named `group.resource.<groupId>` (V1 naming). Result: an admin with all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS gets zero users from search, where before this change the post-filter by `canView(user)` returned them. `/users/count` calls `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`, which returns 0 for an empty set, so a V2 admin who can view members of specific groups sees count 0. Pagination of search is also off, because first/max are applied before the `canView` filter. Suggested fix: for V2, enumerate groups via the resource names (or the groups themselves) and add the group id. Also make the JPA subquery work with V2 resource naming, or skip the pre-filter for V2. Please add a test for `/users/count` and for search with all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS.

Group deletion can now throw UnsupportedOperationException when V1 and V2 features are both enabled

The listener is registered when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1) is on. It calls `management(...)`, which returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is on. `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` now returns `GroupPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (GroupPermissionsV2.java:172-175). Before this PR V2 fell back to V1 `GroupPermissions` there, so deleting a group worked. With both features enabled, `GroupRemovedEvent` now throws and the group delete would fail. Clients already throw on `ClientRemovedEvent` in that combination (ClientPermissionsV2), so this may be accepted. Is the V1+V2 combination unsupported, or should the listener skip group cleanup for V2?

Javadoc inaccuracies in GroupPermissionEvaluator

`requireManageMembers` (line 135) is documented as throwing when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` is false, but the implementation checks `canManageMembers`. The `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` javadoc (line 145) says it returns a 'Stream of IDs' but the method returns `Set<String>`. The `canManageMembers` doc says it returns true if `UserPermissionEvaluator#canManage()` is true, which is correct. The V2-only note on `canManage()` (lines 75-76) documents the VIEW-or-MANAGE behaviour reported as a bug above.

No negative test for write access with view-only permission, and no coverage of count or all-groups members scopes

`testViewGroups` grants VIEW on all groups but never asserts that creating a group or updating a group is still forbidden, which is how the `canManage()` problem in GroupPermissionsV2 went unnoticed. There is also no test for `/users/count` or for user search with an all-groups `view-members` or `manage-members` permission, the paths that use `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`. Other nits: the double semicolon on line 68, a new file with a 2024 copyright header, and trailing whitespace at line 300.

Several providers on the classpath no longer fail; ties are resolved silently by classpath order

The old code threw `IllegalStateException` when more than one `CryptoProvider` was found. The new code sorts by `order()` and takes the first one. `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider` all return 200 (crypto/default DefaultCryptoProvider.java:82-85, crypto/elytron WildFlyElytronProvider.java:75-78, crypto/fips1402 FIPS1402Provider.java:113-116). Each has its own `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider` file. If two of them end up on the classpath, for example the default BC provider next to the FIPS one, the winner is whichever `ServiceLoader` lists first, because `sorted` is stable. Before this change that setup failed at startup. Now a server meant to run in FIPS mode can silently run with the non-FIPS provider. The only trace is a `debug` log (lines 64-70).

The ordering is only needed so the order-100 `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` loses to a real provider. Keep the fail-fast when the top two providers have the same `order()`, and log the ignored providers at `warn` or `info` rather than `debug`.

`order()` is a new abstract method on a public SPI interface

Any `CryptoProvider` outside this repository stops compiling and fails with `AbstractMethodError` at runtime. The four implementations in this repository are all updated. A `default int order() { return 0; }` would keep the SPI compatible, and the in-repo providers could still override it. Related: `CryptoIntegration.java:69` passes a built string to `logger.debugf(String)` as a format string. Use `debug` or pass parameters instead. The message also ends with a trailing ", ".

Dead statements in `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`

Lines 114-115 build two `ASN1Encoder` instances and discard them. They have no effect and look like leftover debugging. Delete them.

`getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns the JDK's PKCS12 provider, and `CryptoIntegration.init` pins this provider for the whole JVM

`BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` is computed from this method (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/util/BouncyIntegration.java:33-39). It will be the name of whichever provider backs the default KeyStore type, usually `SUN`. Callers such as `FIPS1402Provider.getKeyStore` pass `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` to `getInstance`, so a mislabelled provider name is a risk.

`AuthzClient.create` now calls `CryptoIntegration.init`, which stores the provider in a static field that is set only once. If `AuthzClient` is the first caller in a JVM where only authz-client's service file is visible, every later `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature/getKeyFactory/getAesCbcCipher/...` throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")`. Please document this limitation on the class. Alternatively, return `null` from `getBouncyCastleProvider`, which `BouncyIntegration` already handles by falling back to the first security provider.

Test never exercises ES384/ES512 sizes or long-form DER lengths, and only checks a self round-trip

The key is a default `EC` key (P-256, line 42) and is used for ES256, ES384 and ES512 alike. The signature is therefore always about 70-72 bytes of DER, which uses a short-form length. A real ES512 (P-521) signature is about 138-139 bytes and needs the long-form length (`0x81 xx`). That long-form path is in `ASN1Encoder.writeLength` (line 67-79) and `ASN1Decoder.readLength` (line 137-164), and the test never runs it. The 66-byte r/s values and the leading-zero handling in `integerToBytes` for ES512 are not covered either. For ES384/ES512 with a P-256 key the code only left-pads r and s.

The assertion at line 56 compares `rsConcat` with the output of the same provider's decode-encode-decode. An error that is symmetric between encoder and decoder would still pass. Nothing compares the re-encoded DER with the original `sign`, and nothing checks it with `Signature.verify`.

Generate the key on the matching curve for each algorithm (`secp256r1`, `secp384r1`, `secp521r1`). Assert `assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des)` or verify the re-encoded DER. Add a case where r or s has a high bit set or leading zeros, and one where the sequence length is above 127.

The `hamcrest` test dependency added in `authz/client/pom.xml` is also unused by this test.

Malformed DER can raise unchecked exceptions instead of `IOException`

`readLength()` returns -1 for the indefinite form (line 133-135). `readInteger` then calls `read(-1)`, which throws `NegativeArraySizeException` at line 170. `readTagNumber` masks the tag with 0x1f (line 94), so any class or constructed bits are accepted as `INTEGER`/`SEQUENCE`. Trailing bytes after the sequence are ignored, and `integerToBytes` in the provider silently truncates a value longer than `signLength/2`, or turns a negative integer into garbage. The method contract is `throws IOException`. The only in-repo caller, `ECDSASignatureSignerContext`, feeds it the JDK's own signer output, so there is no exposure today. Reject `length < 0` in `readSequence`/`readInteger` and check the tag class and constructed bit.

Reader thread is never joined, so the test can miss failures and leak a spinning thread

The reader thread is started and never joined. `deletedAll.set(true)` is followed at once by `assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty())`. An iteration that is still in flight when the flag flips can fail after the assertion has run, and that exception is lost. If a `remove()` throws in the main thread, `deletedAll` is never set, so the thread loops forever against the shared realm and hammers the server for the rest of the test class. Keep the `Thread` reference, set the flag in a `finally`, call `join()` before asserting, and mark the flag `volatile` or keep the `AtomicBoolean`. An `ExecutorService`/`Future` would also surface the failures cleanly.

Test is timing-dependent and will not reliably reproduce the race

The reader loop has no pause and no guarantee that it overlaps the deletes. Both the 100 sequential creates and the first `groups()` call are done before the deletes begin. The reader's cached top-level group list can also be refreshed from the DB after the last delete, so the stale-cache window may never be hit. The test can pass without the fix, and it gives no signal when that happens. Consider making the overlap deterministic, for example by waiting until the reader has completed at least one call before the first delete. A model-level test of `GroupAdapter` on a deleted group would also pin down the null-handling directly.

Trailing whitespace, a misspelled variable name and a mixed import style

Line 117 is a whitespace-only line. `groupUuuids` has three u's. The test adds `org.hamcrest.Matchers` as a regular import and uses `Matchers.empty()`, while the rest of the class imports Hamcrest matchers statically (`anEmptyMap`, etc.). Use a static import of `empty`. Also, `created` followed by `fail(...)` could be simplified with `assertEquals`/`ApiUtil.getCreatedId` alone.

The fix covers only getSubGroupsCount; the sibling delegations still NPE on a concurrently deleted group

The PR is titled as a fix for concurrent group access causing an NPE. `getSubGroupsCount()` now null-checks `modelSupplier.get()`. The three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still call `modelSupplier.get().…` with no null check. `modelSupplier` is `LazyModel(this::getGroupModel)`, which returns null when the group is gone from the DB (`GroupAdapter.java:298-300`; `LazyModel.java:15-20`). The same race therefore still gives an NPE on any caller that expands sub-groups of a cached group deleted by another transaction. In `GroupUtils.populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups`, `parentModel` from `session.groups().getGroupById` (`GroupUtils.java:47`) is dereferenced at lines 51, 57 and 60 with no null check. A parent deleted concurrently also throws an NPE there. I did not confirm that these paths fail in practice. Please say whether they are intentionally out of scope. If they are not, apply the same null handling to them.

Call to nonexistent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile

`UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition in the repository is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160), and a grep finds no other overload. The `services` module therefore fails to compile, and everything depending on it fails with it. Pass the user, e.g. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`. Also check what the condition means: with the current helper (see the next finding) `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true exactly when the user is set and passkeys are off. That gives the intended behaviour: skip the form only when passkeys are disabled.

`user != null` in isConditionalPasskeysEnabled disables passkeys on the normal (anonymous) login page

The helper returns true only when `user != null`. It now gates both `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` in `authenticate` (line 115) and in `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137). The old code called `fillContextForm` in the anonymous case (`context.getUser() == null` at the old line 137, and the old block in the `else` branch of `authenticate`). With the new condition an anonymous user (no user set yet) never gets `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`, the challenge or the rpId. The login page then has no `//form[@id='webauth']` and no conditional-UI autocomplete. The same applies to the error page after a bad username.

This contradicts the comment at line 114 ("setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled") and the PR's goal of enabling passkeys during re-authentication in addition to normal login. It also breaks the existing tests in this PR: `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` and `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey` open a fresh login and expect the passkey form (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:196). The helper should not depend on the user: `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. If the `user` parameter stays, drop the `!= null` check. If it goes, `UsernameForm` and the two call sites need updating.

Missing @Override on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators

This method overrides the protected hook added in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` (line 128) but has no `@Override`. If the signature drifts, the compiler will not flag it and the override silently stops working. Add `@Override`.

try/catch(Exception) around fail() makes the 'no webauthn form' assertion unclear

`findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException`, which the `catch (Exception)` swallows, so the `assertThat(..., nullValue())` is never evaluated. Any other exception (a driver or timeout error) would also be swallowed and the test would pass. The sibling tests in this PR use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` for this check. Use that here as well (lines 291-297 and 312-318).

Hung flusher process is no longer killed: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for spawn processes

`self.mp_context` is `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` (line 53), so `make_process` at line 105 is `SpawnProcess`. In CPython `SpawnProcess` subclasses `process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.context.Process`, which is what `multiprocessing.Process` names. I could not read the stdlib source from the repo checkout, so this comes from my knowledge of CPython. If that is right, `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False for the real (non-test) flusher. The old `_ensure_process_alive` called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally and caught `ValueError`. Now, on the `hang` cause, the code skips the kill, starts a replacement for the same shards at line 259, and leaves the hung process running. The old and new processes can then both flush the same shard queues and produce duplicate segments. The same check at line 346 in `join()` means `terminate()` is never called either. In `join()` the `break` at line 341 also skips terminate for every remaining process. The fix is to test against the real base class, e.g. `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`. Since the PR adds a CLAUDE.md rule about `isinstance`, the check should be correct. The tests only use threads, so nothing exercises the spawn path.

time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because the test patches time.sleep

Line 15 does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`. That replaces the attribute on the `time` module, so the `time.sleep(0.1)` added here, called as `time.sleep` after `import time`, does nothing. The comment 'Give flusher threads time to process' is false. The extra `step.poll()` does not wait for the flusher threads either. `step.join()` sets `stopped` right away. If the flusher thread has not completed a flush cycle by then, `(msg,) = messages` fails, so the test is still racy. Use the real sleep (e.g. `from time import sleep` before the patch, as test_flusher.py does), or better, poll until `messages` is non-empty with a bounded deadline.

Per-process SpansBuffer changes what spans.buffer.max-flush-segments bounds

`flush_segments` computes `max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(self.assigned_shards))` (buffer.py:382-384). Each flusher process now gets a `SpansBuffer(shards)` containing only its own shards. With one shard per process, each process may flush the full `max-flush-segments` (default 500) per cycle. The consumer-wide total grows to roughly `num_processes × max-flush-segments`, and `any_shard_at_limit` triggers later. Is this intended? If not, scale the option by the number of processes.

get_memory_info is cluster-wide, so it is now repeated once per flusher buffer on every submit

`SpansBuffer.get_memory_info` returns `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)` (buffer.py:375-376). It does not depend on `assigned_shards`. Looping over `self.buffers.values()` therefore queries the whole Redis cluster N times per `submit` and sums N identical copies. The used/available ratio is unchanged, but the cost is multiplied by the number of flusher processes. Call it once, on any one buffer. `submit` runs on the consumer's hot path whenever `max-memory-percentage < 1.0`.

Docstring says one process per shard, but the count is capped by max_processes

The class docstring says 'Creates one process per shard'. The code creates `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` processes. The new CLI option defaults to 1 (consumers/__init__.py:434), so production runs a single process for all shards unless `--flusher-processes` is set. The factory default `None` means one process per shard, which differs from the CLI default. Reword the docstring and make the two defaults consistent or document the difference.

Inconsistent metric tag name and dead code in flusher

`wait_produce` is tagged `"shards"`, while the other new metrics use `"shard"` (lines 185, 195, 244). Dashboards grouped on one name will miss the other. `_create_process_for_shard` (line 127) is unused. `if not process: continue` at line 222 is unreachable because values are always set to a started process. The comment at line 178 ('for all shards') and the one at line 235 ('any shard') describe per-shard behaviour the code does not have, because health is tracked per process.

test_flusher_processes_limit only checks counts and does not cover the new restart or process paths

The test checks `len(flusher.processes)` and the sum of shard counts. It does not check the actual distribution (4 shards over 2 processes should give 2 shards each). It does not flush anything, does not exercise `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts, and does not cover the CLI option wiring. The restart path with per-process `process_restarts` and the spawn `Process` branch are untested, which is how the isinstance issue at flusher.py:254 went unnoticed.

zip(error_ids, events.values()) pairs ids with the wrong events

`nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict containing only the nodes it found. Its order is uncached items first, then cached ones (`items.update(cache_items)`, src/sentry/nodestore/base.py:203-205). It also dedups the input ids. So `events.values()` is neither aligned with `error_ids` nor the same length. When any error event is missing or cached, `zip(error_ids, events.values())` gives the wrong `id` to each event. That is silent. Iterate the dict by key instead, for example `for node_id, data in events.items()`, and keep a node_id→event_id map built from `error_ids`.

Error logs are re-emitted on every page of segments

`on_results=functools.partial(analyze_recording_segments, error_events)` runs once per paginated page of segments, and each run calls a separate Seer request. `gen_request_data` yields all error events that fall before an event's timestamp, and the trailing loop at line 165 yields every error not yet emitted. For a replay spanning more than one page, each page's request therefore contains every error after that page's last event, so those errors are repeated across pages. The errors also appear on pages whose segments they do not belong to. Please confirm that the page size makes this impossible. If it does not, filter errors by the page's timestamp range.

Snuba replay query runs even when error context is disabled

`query_replay_instance` and `process_raw_response` run unconditionally, and `enable_error_context=false` is only checked afterwards (line 87-92). Callers that opt out still pay for a ClickHouse query. That query is also a new failure point, with no try/except, for an endpoint that previously only read segment storage. Move the query inside the `else` branch and wrap it so a Snuba failure degrades to no error context, as `fetch_error_details` does.

ChoiceField rejects the whole batch for any report type outside the 8 listed

The old `BrowserReportType` Literal was never enforced at runtime, so any `type` string was accepted and counted in the metric. Now one report with another type (for example `network-error`, `integrity-violation` or a vendor-specific type) makes the whole POST return 422 (line 115-118). The other valid reports in the same batch are also dropped, including their `raw_report_received` metric. The collector's purpose is to gather these reports, so please either accept any string for `type` or skip invalid items instead of failing the batch.

age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators are incomplete and truthiness-based

Both fields are `required=False` and the validators only run when their own field is present. A report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` therefore passes, although the docstring of `validate_age` says "age is present". The checks `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `.get("timestamp")` are truthiness checks. `age: 0` is valid in the spec, and `age=0` together with `timestamp` passes. Use `"age" in self.initial_data`, and add a `validate()` that requires exactly one of the two.

get_environment_info issues one or two Snuba queries per issue, serially

`issue.get_recommended_event()` runs a Snuba query and, if that finds nothing, `get_latest_event` runs another (src/sentry/models/group.py:870-890). `get_environment()` can add a DB lookup. `get_environment_info` is called inside the list comprehension in both the GitHub and GitLab `build_comment` (github/integration.py:409, gitlab/integration.py:257). The cost is serial latency per issue in the PR-comment task. The broad `except Exception` swallows failures, and it is logged at info with the exception object in `extra`. Consider fetching environments in one query, or at least using `logger.warning` with `exc_info`.

Flagged branch renders an always-empty table, and the flag is not registered

When `use-table-widget-visualization` is on, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and empty `data`. It ignores `tableResults`, `loading`, the title and `getCustomFieldRenderer`, so enabling the flag shows a blank table. The flag string is not registered in any Python feature file (a repo-wide grep finds only this use), so the branch is currently dead. If the intent is a scaffold, add a comment or TODO. Otherwise pass `result.data` and `result.meta` mapped to columns.

"never run" comment may be untrue where the migration already ran

The comment says "This migration had an error and was never run". These are post-deployment migrations, and nothing here shows that no environment (self-hosted, for example) applied 0917 or 0920 with the old body. The no-op is still harmless because 0921 uses a filter-and-create approach that does not depend on earlier rows. Consider rewording the comment to "superseded by 0921" so it stays accurate. The same applies to 0920 line 13.

Analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check

`analytics.record` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` check, so organizations without the feature that hit the endpoint are also counted. Is that intended? If you only want usage by enabled orgs, record after the check. `request.user.id` is None for anonymous or token-only auth, which is fine because `user_id` is `required=False`.

HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only hides attributes while a search query is typed

The early `return sorted` at line 61-63 runs when the search box is empty, which is the default state. The `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` check sits only in the filter below that return (lines 65-69). So `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` show in the span attributes list on first render and disappear once the user types something. They also show again when the box is cleared. Apply the hidden-attribute filter before the search early-return, for example `sorted = sortAttributes(attributes).filter(a => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(a.name))`.

Flex replacement drops align-items and gap from the old FlexBox/Container

The removed `FlexBox` set `display:flex; align-items:center; gap:space(1)`, and `Container` extended it with `justify-content: space-between`. The loaded state at line 93 is now `<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">`. That loses `align="center"` and the gap, so the tab list and the vitals are no longer vertically centred against each other. In `Placeholder`, the second group `<Flex>` (line 27) also loses `align="center"` and `gap={space(1)}`, so the three 100px placeholders sit flush. Pass `align="center"` (and `gap={space(1)}` where it applied) to match the old layout.

Rewritten query drops retry/staleTime options, switches isLoading to isFetching, and the key has no org slug

Three behaviour changes in the move from `useApiQuery` to `useQuery`:
1. `retry: false`, `staleTime: 0` and `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` are gone. The client config at `static/app/utils/queryClient.tsx:19-26` only disables refetch on reconnect and on focus. React Query's default retry therefore applies, so a failed `/trace-items/attributes/` request keeps `isFetching` true through the retry backoff before `error` is set.
2. `isLoading` is now `isFetching`. Any background refetch flips `numberAttributesLoading`/`stringAttributesLoading` in `TraceItemAttributeProvider` (`static/app/views/explore/contexts/traceItemAttributeContext.tsx:43-57`) to true. Before, only the initial load did.
3. The key `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]` has no organization slug. The slug is only read inside `queryFn` (`useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:78`). Two orgs with identical project ids, datetime and item type share a cache entry, and the other org's attributes show while the refetch runs.
Add `retry: false` and `staleTime: 0` to keep the old behaviour, and include `organization.slug` in the key.

Truthiness check on custom cell contradicts the documented 'undefined falls back' contract

The story (tableWidgetVisualization.stories.tsx:113) and the prop JSDoc say the default renderer runs when the custom renderer returns `undefined`. Lines 32 and 71 use `if (cell)`, so a custom renderer that returns `0`, `''` or `false` is also overridden by the default renderer. A count cell of `0` rendered by a custom function silently falls back. Use `cell !== undefined`. Related: the `!tableData?.meta` branch at line 76 is unreachable because `meta` is required on `TabularData`.

Flex.Item grow={1} is not equivalent to the removed `flex: 1`

The removed FlexContainer used `flex: 1`, which is `1 1 0%`. `Flex.Item grow={1}` renders `flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: auto` (static/app/components/core/layout/flex.tsx:35-46). With a basis of auto, a long description or feature list starts from its max-content width, and the sibling `Metadata` block (which defaults to flex-shrink 1, integrationLayout.tsx:362-370) is shrunk in proportion to it. With `flex: 1` the description only took the space left over after Metadata was sized. This can change the layout of the integration detail header. `Flex.Item` accepts a `flex` prop, so `<Flex.Item flex="1">` keeps the old behavior.

Environment assertions depend on Snuba data, but TestGetCommentBody is not a SnubaTestCase

`get_comment_body` now calls `get_environment_info`, which calls `issue.get_recommended_event()`. That queries Snuba (src/sentry/models/group.py:274-290). Any failure is swallowed and returns an empty string (commit_context.py:584-597). `test_simple` now expects ` in `dev`` and ` in `prod`` in the output. `TestGetCommentBody` derives from `GithubCommentTestCase(IntegrationTestCase)` with no `SnubaTestCase`. The tracker's per-partition state (`last_committed`, outstanding offsets) must also be reset when partitions are revoked.
